questions.q: What does the pipeline graph view show?
options: Only error messages, with no structural information
Only the final gold table, with no upstream detail
Each @dlt.table/@dlt.view as a node, with arrows for the dependencies inferred from dlt.read()/dlt.read_stream() calls, updated live per run
A static diagram that never updates after the pipeline is first defined
questions.explain: This is the exact bronze->silver->gold structure from Lesson 44's lineage diagram, scoped to one pipeline's execution.

questions.q: What do per-table metrics in the pipeline UI combine?
options: Only row counts, with no relationship to expectations
Only Unity Catalog access grants for that table
Rows processed this run, plus expectation pass/fail counts (Lesson 52) for that table, shown together in one place
Only the table's storage size on disk
questions.explain: This combines what Lesson 36's separate quality table and Lesson 11's job run history tracked separately, now together.

questions.q: Why is the event log described as "nothing exotic" to query?
options: It's stored in a format unrelated to Delta Lake
It can only be viewed through the UI, never queried directly
It's a real, queryable Delta table — exactly Chapter 2's material — so it can be queried with plain SQL like any other table
It requires a completely new, specialized query language
questions.explain: This turns "did something break, and where" into a real SQL query, filterable and joinable like any other table.

questions.q: What does the event log record?
options: Only successful runs, never failures
Every event across every run — which tables updated, which expectations failed, which run raised an error, and when
Only Unity Catalog grant/revoke actions
Only the pipeline's initial creation, not ongoing runs
questions.explain: This is a real, queryable Delta table, not just a UI-only log.

questions.q: What's the recommended order for investigating a pipeline failure?
options: Always start by querying the event log with no other context
Graph view first (which table failed), then per-table metrics (did expectations catch it?), then the event log (the actual error message)
There's no recommended order; any starting point works equally well
Only check Unity Catalog permissions, regardless of the failure type
questions.explain: This ordered approach is the practical answer to "what broke and where" after a failure has already occurred.
